# fptcloud_backup_native_volume_job_run (Resource)

Runs a Backup Native volume backup job once, outside its schedule, the same operation as "Start backup" in the portal. Applying the resource checks the job's status, starts the run and waits for it to end. A job that is still running a backup, a restore or a change fails the apply at once, without starting a run. Destroying the resource only removes it from state. Change a value in `triggers` to run the backup again. Once the run has started, the resource is saved whatever the outcome, and the next apply does not run it again. A failed run, a timeout or an interrupted apply (Ctrl+C) ends the apply with a warning, not an error, and stores the outcome in `status` and `message`. The backup goes on without Terraform after a timeout or an interrupt; each later plan or apply reads the job's status and stores the outcome once the run ends. That status may come from a later scheduled run of the same job. Only interrupt an apply once: a second Ctrl+C stops Terraform before it saves the run, and the next apply starts another. A job with one volume may be retried by the backend after a failed run. When the job stays in `pending`, the apply runs out its timeout; only a later run or the backend clears that state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Runs fptcloud_backup_native_volume_job.data once and waits for the run to end.
# Any value works and a new value runs it again. A request time, as below, is
# recommended so the state records when each run was requested. Avoid
# timestamp(): it changes on every plan and runs a backup on every apply.
resource "fptcloud_backup_native_volume_job_run" "data" {
  vpc_id   = var.vpc_id
  job_id   = fptcloud_backup_native_volume_job.data.id
  triggers = { run = "2026-10-26 09:00:00" }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `job_id` (String) ID of the backup job to run, the `id` of a `fptcloud_backup_native_volume_job`.
- `vpc_id` (String) ID of the VPC that owns the backup job.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `triggers` (Map of String) Values that run the backup again when they change, which no other argument can express because every other argument stays equal. Any string works; only a change matters. We recommend the time you ask for the action, in the form `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, for example `2026-10-26 09:00:00`, so the state records when each one was requested. Avoid `timestamp()`: it changes on every plan and repeats the action on every apply.

### Read-Only

- `finished_at` (String) When the provider saw the run end, RFC 3339 UTC.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `message` (String) Why the action did not succeed, or why the provider stopped waiting for it. Empty after a success.
- `started_at` (String) When the provider started the run, RFC 3339 UTC.
- `status` (String) The job's status when the run ended: `Success` or `success` after a successful run, the API's failure status (`Failed` or `error` for a VM job, `error` for a volume job) after a failed one. The provider stores its own value when the API has none to give: `tf_timeout` when the provider stopped waiting before the action ended, `tf_interrupted` when the apply was interrupted while it waited, `tf_failed` when the action failed without an API status. A plan or apply checks `tf_timeout` and `tf_interrupted` again and replaces them with the API's status once the action ends.
